whatIsIt.eli5: YOLOv13's 'group finder'. It looks at three map sizes together and finds groups of pixels that belong together, even far apart, then shares what each group knows.
whatIsIt.simple: Takes P3, P4 and P5, brings them to P4 size and joins them. Then a CSP-style block runs: two branches use a hypergraph (learned groups of pixels called hyperedges) to pass information between all pixels in a group, and a third branch uses depthwise-separable blocks for local detail.
whatIsIt.engineer: FuseModule(P3↓, P4, P5↑) → cv1 (1×1, 3c) → chunk(3); branch1/branch2 = C3AH (AdaHGComputation) on chunk 1; DSC3k chain on chunk 3; cat[y0, h1, y2, m…, h2] → cv2. Learnable hyperedge prototypes + context; message passing via two bmm's (linear in N).

whyExists.eli5: Pairs of spots are not enough; whole groups (like all leaves of one weed) should talk at once.
whyExists.simple: The paper argues that convolutions see only nearby pixels and self-attention only models pairs, while hypergraphs capture high-order relations among many pixels across scales, at linear cost.
whyExists.engineer: High-order, cross-scale correlation modelling with linear-complexity hypergraph message passing (paper §3.2).

eli5: Bring the three map sizes to one size and stack them.
Learn a few groups; each pixel decides how much it belongs to each group.
Each group collects notes from its pixels, then gives them back.
Mix with local helpers and summarize.
simple: Fuse: P3 is average-pooled down, P5 upsampled, both joined with P4; 1×1 Conv.
Two hypergraph branches (C3AH) on the middle part: build hyperedges from the content, compute each pixel's soft membership, gather to hyperedges, scatter back.
A chain of DS-C3k blocks on the third part.
Join everything and mix with a 1×1 Conv.
engineer: Hyperedges: 8 in the YAML; parse_model halves them for n (4) and ×1.5 for x (12).
AdaHyperedgeGen: prototypes = base + Linear(mean‖max context); logits = (XW)·protoᵀ/√d averaged over heads; softmax over N.
HGConv: He = GELU(Lin(Aᵀ X)); X' = GELU(Lin(A·He)) + X.

example.eli5: In YOLOv13n it works on the 40×40 size.
example.simple: YOLOv13n layer 9: inputs from layers 4, 6, 8; output 128 channels at 40×40; 4 hyperedges; 273,536 parameters.

typicalPositions.eli5: Between the backbone and the mixing part.
typicalPositions.simple: Once, right after the backbone, reading P3, P4 and P5.
typicalPositions.engineer: Neck entry; its output feeds all FullPAD tunnels.
